adaptive_test_time_compute.description: Methods that allocate more compute to harder inputs
key_works: Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute (Snell et al., 2024)
adaptive_test_time_compute.distinction: ASAR measures quality of heterogeneous cognitive operations, not homogeneous compute steps. Test-time compute scales amount; ASAR studies composition and ordering of qualitatively different operations.
adaptive_test_time_compute.unique_to_asar: Counterfactual measurement of operation-type value; temporal complementarity between operation types

adaptive_retrieval.description: Systems that decide when and what to retrieve
adaptive_retrieval.distinction: Adaptive retrieval is one of several cognitive operations in ASAR. ASAR studies the interaction between retrieval and non-retrieval operations (hypothesis generation, reasoning, attack). Retrieval alone is a component, not the research object.
adaptive_retrieval.unique_to_asar: Multi-operation composition; complementarity between retrieval and other cognitive types

process_reward_models.description: Models that score intermediate reasoning steps
key_works: Lightman et al. (2024) — step-level reward in math
process_reward_models.distinction: PRMs evaluate steps within a homogeneous reasoning chain. ASAR evaluates heterogeneous cognitive operations (retrieve, hypothesize, attack, reason) and their interactions. PRMs score quality; ASAR measures downstream epistemic gain.
process_reward_models.unique_to_asar: Operations differ in kind, not just quality; complementarity/interference between operations

reasoning_trajectory_evaluation.description: Evaluating and selecting among reasoning paths
reasoning_trajectory_evaluation.distinction: ToT/GoT branch within a single operation type (reasoning). ASAR composes across operation types. The search space is qualitatively different: operation-type sequences vs reasoning-step trees.
reasoning_trajectory_evaluation.shared: Multi-path evaluation, search over cognitive strategies

hierarchical_llm_planning.distinction: Hierarchical planning selects sub-tasks. ASAR measures the value of cognitive operation sequences independently of hierarchical decomposition. The benchmark measures operation-level effects, not task-level planning.
hierarchical_llm_planning.shared: Multi-level decision making about cognitive strategies

agent_planning_search_decoupling.description: Separating planning from execution in agents
agent_planning_search_decoupling.distinction: These decouple planning from execution. ASAR decouples generation from verification (invariant 4) and studies the value of different operation orderings. The benchmark measures why certain orderings outperform others.
agent_planning_search_decoupling.unique_to_asar: Systematic complementarity measurement; controlled epistemic environment

learned_skills_options.description: Option/skill frameworks in RL and agents
learned_skills_options.distinction: Options/skills are learned from reward. ASAR cognitive motifs are empirically derived from sequence analysis. The research question is whether motif composition is valuable, not whether motifs can be learned.
learned_skills_options.shared: Temporal abstraction of primitive actions into reusable sequences
learned_skills_options.unique_to_asar: Epistemic (rather than reward-based) evaluation; counterfactual measurement of motif value

reasoning_strategy_routing.description: Routing inputs to different reasoning strategies
reasoning_strategy_routing.distinction: Strategy routing selects a strategy at input time. ASAR studies sequential composition of operations within a single task. The temporal dimension (what comes after what) is the key research object.
reasoning_strategy_routing.unique_to_asar: Sequential composition; temporal complementarity; order effects

long_horizon_search_agents.distinction: These are applied agent systems. ASAR provides a controlled benchmark for understanding why certain cognitive sequences work. The distinction is scientific instrument vs. engineering system.
long_horizon_search_agents.unique_to_asar: Controlled epistemic environment with ground truth; mechanism measurement

metacognitive_agents.description: Agents with explicit self-monitoring and strategy adjustment
metacognitive_agents.distinction: Metacognitive agents add self-reflection loops. ASAR asks whether metacognitive control (adaptive operation selection) actually helps, and found it currently does NOT outperform fixed sequences. This negative result is itself a contribution.
metacognitive_agents.unique_to_asar: Quantified failure of adaptive metacognitive control; adaptivity gap measurement

dynamic_reasoning_graphs.distinction: Dynamic graphs construct reasoning structures. ASAR measures the value of the construction process itself — which operations to use and in what order. The graph is an artifact; the construction sequence is the research object.
dynamic_reasoning_graphs.unique_to_asar: Process-level measurement; temporal complementarity of construction operations

tool_use_scheduling.description: Scheduling tool calls in LLM agents
tool_use_scheduling.distinction: Tool scheduling decides when to call external tools. ASAR's cognitive operations are analogous to tool types, but the benchmark measures the epistemic value of operation sequences, not tool call efficiency. The operations differ in cognitive kind, not just API endpoint.
tool_use_scheduling.unique_to_asar: Epistemic quality measurement; temporal complementarity between operation types
